text: Evolutionary biologists are interested in knowing how old the universe is. According to one estimate, the universe is almost 20 billion years old. The elements hydrogen and helium are supposed to appear immediately after the Big Bang. The earth is supposed to have been formed about 4.5 billion years back.

There are many speculations and ideas about the origin of life. One is that life appeared from inanimate matter such as clay minerals repeatedly, rather than a one-time event. S. L. Miller performed an experiment and proved that organic monomers can be synthesised under conditions assumed to be similar to primitive earth.

Palaeontological studies, or the fossil studies, indicate gradual sequence of evolution. Fossils are generally found in sedimentary rocks, and based on dating of rocks and fossils one gets a clue about their age and succession. Fossils found in deeper layers are supposed to be more ancient compared to those found in upper layers.

Darwin's finches, a group of fourteen closely related species of birds collected by Darwin from Galapagos Islands, provide a good example of adaptive radiation, where a group of closely related species arises from a common ancestor and evolves different structures suited to the different needs, in this case different beaks for different eating habits.

Darwin's theory of natural selection states that nature selects the fit over the unfit organisms on the basis of characteristics related to adaptation. Heritable variations occur in organisms, more individuals are produced than can survive, and those better adapted to the environment leave more progeny than others, resulting in natural selection.

A diploid population, that is sexually reproducing, consists of a pool of genes, the gene pool, made up of alleles that determine all the characteristics of that population. The Hardy-Weinberg principle states that allele frequencies in a population are stable and are constant from generation to generation, and the gene pool remains constant; this is called genetic equilibrium. The sum total of all allelic frequencies is 1.

Lamarck, based on his studies on invertebrates, postulated that body parts or organs of an animal, which are used more often, are more developed; disuse leads them to degenerate, and these changes acquired during the lifetime of an individual are inherited by the next generation, illustrated by the example of the long neck of the giraffe arising from stretching to feed on tall trees. This idea of inheritance of acquired characters is referred to as Lamarckism.

India, with only 2.4 per cent of the world's land area, accounts for nearly 8.1 per cent of the global species diversity, which has earned the country a place among the twelve mega diversity countries of the world.

According to IUCN, there are 34 globally recognised biodiversity hotspots, and of these, four are present in India, namely, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, the Himalaya, the Indo-Burma region and Sundaland, covering our Northeast and the Nicobar group of islands.

India has a network of protected areas, including 90 national parks and 448 wildlife sanctuaries, and in addition, the Government of India has designated 18 biosphere reserves for protecting representative ecosystems.
